title: Catch the ABA problem with a stamped reference

blocks.text: A plain compare-and-set only asks *is the value still what I read?* If another thread changed it from `A` to `B` and back to `A` in between, the CAS succeeds although the value did change: the **ABA problem**. The page's fix is `AtomicStampedReference`, which pairs the reference with an integer **stamp** (a version) and compares both.
Write `VersionedValue`, a value with a stamp that starts at 0:

items: `set(newValue)` stores the value and adds one to the stamp;

`compareAndSet(expectedValue, expectedStamp, newValue)` succeeds only if **both** still match (the value by reference, as a CAS does); then it stores `newValue`, adds one to the stamp and returns `true`. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns `false`.

blocks.text: The examples use string literals, which are the same reference each time.

cases.says: set changes the value and bumps the stamp, and a compare-and-set with the current value and stamp succeeds.
After A to B and back to A, a compare-and-set that expects A with the old stamp fails.
A compare-and-set with a stale stamp leaves both the value and the stamp as they were.
The value is compared by reference: an equal String that is a different object does not match.

concepts: A CAS cannot see a value that changed from A to B and back; AtomicStampedReference pairs it with a stamp.
